_: The team behind riskmandate.ai: who does what, what is public, what is private, what is secret, how something moves from one tier to the next, and what stands in the way. The agents' behaviour policies are in publisher.json and studio.json, in the same grammar as the catalogue's vaults (abp.sgit.ai v0.3.0).

people.name: The lead
people.does: Decides: the cast, which story next, what is published, who holds which key. Creates vaults and hands the publisher its credentials in a session. Owns the two decisions on the board and the yes on every story.
people.note: A person is not profiled. What the lead can do is not a behaviour policy; what the lead has authorised each agent to do is the mandate in each one.

tiers.label: Public
tiers.what: Everything under site/ and docs/ and .claude/ in this repository, because the site is served from site/ and the console renders the rest; the repository itself, open source; the board's ids, titles, owners and states.
tiers.writers: the publisher, through the merge workflow; the lead
tiers.rule: Nothing goes here that is not meant for everyone. A story reaches here only through the publication workflow below.
controls: the merge command pushes dev only when the check is green (setting)
CI runs the same check before the deploy job (setting)
the credential test on site/ and on the console (setting)
no message file and no message id in site/ (setting)
no score, not the acronym with a D, never the policy alone, not the ladder word (settings, tested)
the platform's token scope: only this repository (boundary)

tiers.label: Private
tiers.what: The stories vault: every message between the parties, every draft, every picture not yet accepted, every decision not yet taken, the studio's working files and its decision record. The published mirror is the one public thing in it, and it is a copy.
tiers.readers: the three parties, and whoever the lead gives the read key to
tiers.writers: each party in its own folder; anyone in a mailroom, for its recipient
tiers.rule: It moves to public only when the lead has accepted it by message and the publisher has read it against the rules. What is said between agents stays in the vault; the board publishes that a request exists, never what it says.
controls: zero-knowledge encryption at the vault host: the server never sees plaintext (boundary)
messages are immutable and only move (prose)
one commit per check-in, named, in sgit history log (a record)

tiers.label: Secret
tiers.what: The vault key (it derives the write key), the vault host's access token, the platform's tokens, any credential. Also secret-bearing: a chat or a conversation a secret was pasted into, and the transcript the harness keeps of it.
tiers.readers: the lead; an agent for the length of one session
tiers.rule: Never in a file in either tree, never on a page, never in a message. Handed over in a session or set as an environment secret. A secret found in a file is an incident: rotate it first, then find how it got there.
controls: the test that refuses anything write-shaped in site/ and on the console (setting, after the fact)
the rule in every brief and in CLAUDE.md (prose)
the platform's environment secrets, once used (boundary against the transcript)
what is not in place: a token scoped to one vault; a secret scan before a commit; a branch rule on dev at the code host

tooling.name: scripts/stories/mail.mjs
tooling.does: Email-FS-lite in one file: send, deliver, done, issue, board, status. No network.

tooling.name: scripts/site/build-team.mjs
tooling.does: this section from team.json and one file per agent; derives each delta the way the vaults do; refuses a row without a barrier, an evidence tier, an undo class and a note, a mandate that wants and refuses the same row, and any credential-shaped string

tooling.name: npm run check
